newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products firm with NYMEX, refinery.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products firm with NYMEX, refinery.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices firmed moderately late Thursday, traders said, lifted by a combination of higher NYMEX prices and news of a Los Angeles-area refinery fire, the second in 10 days.
January NYMEX crude settled 51 cents higher at $23.84 a barrel, on forecasts of colder temperatures and a technical rebound after Wednesday price collapse.
Refined products followed crude, with Dec unleaded gasoline up 1.65 cents a gallon to 67.04 cents, and "heat" rising 1.76 cents a gallon to 73.85 cents.
"It looks like its's going to follow through tomorrow," a trader said, noting ACCESS overnight prices rose another 0.20 cent. He said that gave traders extra incentive to buy Friday.
Los Angeles offers of conventional regular gasoline rose two cents to 60.50 cents a gallon late.
Fueling the price rises was news of a fire at Mobil's 130,000 barrel-per-day refinery in a suburb south of Los Angeles.
The fire was the second L.A.-area refinery blaze in 10 day. On November 11, a hydrotreater burned at Texaco's nearby refinery.
The Mobil plant makes 105,000 barrels-per-day of gasoline and traders speculated they would need to buy spot product.

Offers for L.A. California Air Resources Board (CARB) gasoline strengthened 1.50 cents to 64 cents a gallon. Bay area grades were three cents cheaper, as supply was seen more adequate with fewer refineries down, traders said.
Distillates firmed in L.A. and San Francisco, on rumors of increased exports from the West Coast.
Offers for jet fuel in L.A. rose two cents to 72/73 cents a gallon, with Bay material notionally the same. Low sulphur diesel offers also rose one cent to 69 cents.
